title: Xavier, Southern University and languages
summary: Academic courses in French, German and Spanish, useful when touring overseas.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: What year were you at Xavier?
I was about, uh, 50, I think 50, no, no, I was in the 40s. Uh, about 49, 50, 40, around 50, yeah, 50 and 51.
And you studied just music at Xavier?

No, well I couldn't take a full course because I was playing music at night. I took French. I had, I took 12 hours of French. And science. Because those are something that I'd have to take if I, I didn't want to take, I didn't take any musical courses. I played with the band. But I wanted to try to get those academic courses out of the way first.
So were you, were you going for a degree at Xavier? To get a, to get a degree or was it?

Um, yes and no. Uh, see I never did worry about having a degree. Although I've gone to different schools to learn what I figure is necessary for a trumpet player, I mean a musician to know. Right. I got, I got, I had 12 hours of, uh, French at Xavier. Then I had 12 hours of Germany, of German at, uh, Suno. Uh-huh. And, uh, nine I was, uh, uh, Spanish at Suno.
So you have a lot of foreign languages.

Yeah. But see now, like, what happened, I used to go, go, go, go overseas a lot. Uh-huh. And when I go overseas, I would, uh, I wasn't lost, I could say, uh, whatever I wanted to say, you know. Uh-huh. Now like, when I go over there now, I have to, uh, just review my tapes. I have tapes of all those courses that I have.
